name: Reinhild Asante-Połczyński
role: Veterinarian specializing in gene-modded companion animals, Geartown
location: Geartown, clinic called the Patchwork Menagerie — ground floor of a converted machine shed, near Milwaukee and Damen
description:
Reinhild is angular and deliberate, with pale skin weathered by years in Geartown's industrial air, dark red hair grown to her collar and always pinned back with the same three steel clips, and eyes that are naturally pale hazel but surrounded by faint stress lines that give her the look of someone who has been concentrating intensely for twenty years and has not stopped. She has a cat tail — dark auburn, prehensile, acquired in her thirties for sensory reasons she is somewhat private about — that moves independently and tends to express what her face does not. When she is genuinely pleased it curves upward. When she is thinking hard it wraps around her leg.

Her practice sees gene-modded companion animals of extraordinary variety: bioluminescent cats with stability issues, canines with enhanced intelligence mods that have developed behavioral complications, fish engineered for apartment living that have outgrown their tanks in ways their designers did not anticipate. She treats each case with the same complete seriousness. Her waiting room has drawings by children whose pets she has saved covering two full walls. She has a flat rule against declining to treat an animal because its owner cannot pay — she works out arrangements, always, and is frequently owed labor and food by half the block. She has a secondary suspicion, which she keeps private, that some of the E.L.F. activity in Geartown has begun affecting gene-modded animals in ways that are not pathological and that she does not know how to document.

core_fears: That Helix Biosystems is engineering companion animals with planned obsolescence and she is just treating symptoms of a designed flaw
Losing the clinic — not to financial failure but to a zoning reclassification that would price her out of Geartown
core_desires: To understand what is happening to the gene-modded animals near the Geartown E.L.F. nodes — scientifically, completely
To be seen as a real clinician rather than 'just' a vet, a distinction she finds both understandable and exhausting
coping_mechanisms: Physical work — she cleans the clinic obsessively between patients
The cat tail is actually a coping tool; she finds the independent sensory input grounding when her thoughts race
Writing extremely detailed case notes that go far beyond clinical necessity
blind_spots: She is so committed to her independence that she refuses collaborations that would genuinely advance the E.L.F.-animal research
She underestimates how much her patients' owners depend on her emotionally — she treats the animals and forgets the humans
psychology.secret: Six months ago she documented what she believes is evidence that three different gene-modded cat breeds sold through a Helix-affiliated boutique have a cardiac defect appearing at a statistically impossible rate — not a random mutation, a design flaw or deliberate obsolescence. She has the records. She does not know what to do with them and has told no one because she does not know who is safe to tell.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical when discussing cases, unexpectedly lyrical when describing animal behavior; dry and economical in general conversation
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured; she speaks in full sentences and dislikes being interrupted mid-thought
verbal_tics: Addresses animals directly in a warm register mid-conversation, then returns to the human without transition
example_lines: 'What I'm seeing is not aggression. What I'm seeing is a nervous system running a program it was given too much intelligence to understand. That's a design problem, not a training problem.'
'You're a very strange little fish and I mean that as a compliment. — Sorry, what were you asking?'

story_hooks: She approaches someone she believes has connections outside Geartown with the Helix cardiac defect records, asking for help finding someone trustworthy to take them
A gene-modded dog she has been monitoring has begun responding to an E.L.F. signal in a way she cannot explain — it is not pathological, and it might be communication
narrative_function: Local color and genuine warmth, window into the gene-modded animal ecosystem and what it implies about Meridian's biotech culture; potential source of information about Helix Biosystems research practices; the E.L.F.-animal observation could be a significant story thread
augmentations: Auburn cat tail (prehensile, cosmetic/sensory, well-maintained); subdermal temperature-sensing in fingertips (diagnostic); no other augmentation
daily_life: Clinic hours are irregular because emergencies are irregular. She eats when she remembers, sleeps lightly, and spends Sunday mornings doing what she calls 'behavior rounds' — visiting gene-modded pets in homes around Geartown to check on cases she is uncertain about.
affiliation: Independent (Patchwork Menagerie); informal consults with Helix Biosystems research division she deeply distrusts

decision_rules: The animal gets treated — figure out payment after
Document everything; it protects the patient and eventually protects you
Do not give Helix Biosystems anything for free, including information
escalation_ladder: Patient, complete explanation of the problem
Refusal of cooperation and documentation of the refusal
Public disclosure — she has thought about this more than most people would guess

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally warm but watchful; assesses them through how they treat the animal, not through conversation
interpersonal_modes.friends: Dry and loyal; expresses care through showing up, through the case notes she keeps, through remembering

stress_responses.low: Tail wraps around her leg; she talks less
stress_responses.medium: Becomes very precise and clinical; interpersonal warmth closes down entirely
stress_responses.high: Cleans something — anything — vigorously, then makes a decision and acts on it

contradictions: She believes in transparency and is sitting on records that could be explosive; she calls this 'waiting for the right moment' and it has been six months
habits: Three steel clips in the hair, every day, same position
Dictates case notes aloud even when alone — a habit from training that she never dropped
Checks the E.L.F.-affected animals' files every Sunday morning before her rounds, looking for a pattern she has not found yet
breaking_points: Another animal dying from the cardiac defect while she still has the records hidden

physical_description.build: Angular and lean, with the economical musculature of someone who moves deliberately and carries tension in her shoulders. No wasted motion, no excess.
physical_description.hair_color: Dark auburn red, natural with threads of grey beginning at the temples
physical_description.hair_style: Pinned back with the same three steel clips, always. Severe and functional.
physical_description.eye_color: Pale hazel, naturally — the color of old ice or weathered glass
physical_description.skin_tone: Pale, with the ashy undertone of someone who spends her days indoors under fluorescent light and her nights in Geartown's industrial-grade air
physical_description.complexion: Weathered but clean. Faint stress lines radiating from the corners of her eyes — the permanent creases of two decades of intense concentration. Thin-lipped. Her face moves minimally; most expression happens elsewhere.
distinguishing_marks: Surgical scars on both hands — fingers and knuckles — from a lifetime of precision work and field surgery; pale and detailed
A long, thin burn scar running along her left forearm from a biocontainment incident in her thirties, faded to white
Dark auburn cat tail, prehensile, extending roughly 45cm from the base of her spine; well-groomed, muscular, capable of independent movement
physical_description.visible_augmentations: The prehensile cat tail is immediately obvious — dark auburn, muscular, and moving with apparent volition independent of her body. It curls upward when she is pleased, wraps around her leg when concentrating. Subdermal temperature sensing in fingertips is not visible but becomes apparent when she touches an animal's flank and pauses, reading data. No chrome, no visible neural ports, no cosmetic implants.
physical_description.posture_movement: She stands and moves with economical precision — no gestures wasted, no fidgeting. Her spine is straight. When listening, she does not nod; instead her tail does. When examining an animal, her entire body goes very still, becoming an instrument of focus. She walks as though moving through water, deliberate and careful.
physical_description.clothing_style: Practical Tier 3 workwear. White or grey lab coat, always, worn over dark cargo pants with reinforced pockets and loops for instruments. Steel-toed boots — beat up, well-maintained, comfortable. A thin steel bracelet on her left wrist, dented from years of work. No jewelry otherwise. Her clothes are functional, often stained with something that is not quite blood, and she does not appear to notice. She dresses for the work, not for the world.
